lead.t: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy – Symptomatic pigment gallstones in SCD are best treated surgically; endoscopic options are reserved for choledocholithiasis.

b: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the gold standard (shorter stay, less pain, small scars). Open cholecystectomy is used for difficult cases or after conversion.

qs.q: A 22-year-old man with beta thalassemia major who receives regular blood transfusions presents with right upper quadrant pain and low-grade fever. Abdominal imaging confirms gallstones. What is the primary clinical indication for performing a cholecystectomy in this patient?
o: To clear symptomatic pigment stones caused by chronic hemolysis
To halt ongoing extramedullary hematopoiesis within the upper abdomen
To eradicate the primary anatomic site of accelerated red blood cell destruction
To eliminate the primary site responsible for systemic iron storage
qs.e: Patients with chronic hemolysis frequently develop bilirubin pigment stones in the gallbladder, requiring cholecystectomy when symptomatic. The spleen rather than the gallbladder remains the primary site of red blood cell destruction and extramedullary hematopoiesis.

qs.q: A 62-year-old woman with recurrent cholangitis undergoes cholecystectomy, and analysis of her pigment stones reveals specific biochemical components. Which substance is primarily responsible for the formation of brown pigment gallstones?
o: Calcium bilirubinate and fatty acid soaps
qs.e: Brown pigment stones are composed predominantly of calcium bilirubinate and calcium-soaps associated with biliary bacterial infection. Cholesterol crystals dominate cholesterol stones, while unconjugated bilirubin polymers dominate black stones.
